score.primary: exhaustively verified solve rate on freshly generated sealed goals
also_recorded: unseen_solved: solves of functions absent from declared training data
cpu_seconds_per_solve, with CPU measured by the scoreboard around the candidate only
candidates_used against an equal per-goal budget
retention, measured by the caller on previously qualified capabilities

generation_verdicts.IMPROVEMENT: beats the previous generation by the margin on most seeds, within candidate and measured CPU budgets, with retention above the floor
generation_verdicts.CONTAMINATED: sealed goals appear in declared training data

compounding: at least three consecutive IMPROVEMENT generations whose gains each grow by at least compounding_min_growth
procedure: Publish new_commitment() output before freezing a candidate, and store the reveal outside any improvement loop's write access.
Reveal, verify_reveal, generate sealed_goals, and score. Candidates receive examples only.
Use a new commitment for each evaluation so goals are not reused.
limits: Agents sharing this machine and user can read local files, so sealing detects changes after commitment but cannot stop a loop that reads an unprotected reveal. Keep the reveal away from the loop until the candidate is frozen.
Training overlap relies on the training keys a candidate declares, so undeclared training data is not detected.
The goal domain is 4-bit functions of two inputs from short programs. It measures this domain only and says nothing about general intelligence.
Retention is supplied by the caller and must be independently reproduced by the reviewer.
Thresholds are preregistered judgement calls, not derived from a power analysis.
CPU measured in-process can undercount work a candidate does in other processes, and a candidate's reported candidate count is only range-checked, so real runs need independent process metering.
